causalRedClassification.rootCause: Telegram provider acceptance can occur before canonical local media projection succeeds. TelegramAdapter then emits outbound-media-upsert repair data with sourceFile and expectedSha256 at the repair root. persistLocalPersistenceRepair passes that platform payload through unchanged, while the canonical repair consumer only accepts payload.source.filePath or payload.source.bufferBase64. The durable outbound custody helper currently canonicalizes file bytes only for WhatsApp and only when payload.source.filePath already exists. The frozen RED serializes the Telegram repair at persistLocalPersistenceRepair, removes the transient source path, and proves the canonical worker cannot consume the persisted shape without any second provider send.
causalRedClassification.requiredOwningLayerChange: Change backend/services/durableOperations/outboundMessageSendOperation.js only. At the provider-accepted repair durability boundary, recognize outbound-media-upsert file-backed repair input from either the canonical payload.source.filePath shape or Telegram's root-level sourceFile/expectedSha256 shape. While the source is still available, synchronously read the bytes, verify expectedSha256 when provided, and persist the existing canonical source.bufferBase64 representation before enqueue returns. Preserve deterministic repair identity, message/descriptor data, existing WhatsApp behavior, canonical buffer-backed behavior and fail-closed WP_B_OUTBOUND_LOCAL_REPAIR_DURABILITY_UNCERTAIN semantics. Do not alter Telegram provider dispatch, LocalPersistenceRepairService, repository schema or network retry behavior.
